topics.topic: How to state the OperationBinding ordering requirement without an unclassified tuple expression
questions: State the OperationBinding ordering requirement as classified prose without the tuple expression `(direction, name)` or move the ordering policy into an imported constant and name that constant.
Replace the tuple-like expression with classified prose, for example by requiring OperationBinding ports to be ordered first by direction and then by name.
This passage must state the OperationBinding port-ordering requirement as classified prose without the tuple expression `(direction, name)`.

quotes: record_change: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] A content record is written with its order-free lists in the order content_identity sorts them before hashing — ports by (direction, name), flow nodes by node_id, flow edges by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port), flow constants by (to_node, to_port) — never in the order a caller submitted them, so equal content submitted in another order is the same record with the same lists, and every read returns those lists in that order; an OperationBinding, a lifecycle record, writes its inputs and outputs the same way, ports by (direction, name), the name order A08 checks a proposal's ports in; every other list, and every JSON value, keeps its order.
judgement.why: The newly added OperationBinding requirement uses the tuple expression `(direction, name)` where the standard requires the call-site requirement to remain classified prose without expressions.

quotes: record_change: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] A content record is written with its order-free lists in the order content_identity sorts them before hashing — ports by (direction, name), flow nodes by node_id, flow edges by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port), flow constants by (to_node, to_port) — never in the order a caller submitted them, so equal content submitted in another order is the same record with the same lists, and every read returns those lists in that order; an OperationBinding, a lifecycle record, writes its inputs and outputs the same way, ports by (direction, name), the name order A08 checks a proposal's ports in; every other list, and every JSON value, keeps its order.
judgement.why: The positive note names content_identity as the source of required ordering even though that symbol is absent from the module's declared import surface, so the dependency must be declared or the textual need removed.

topics.topic: Whether ports must be canonicalized by direction then name rather than preserving caller order
questions: Replace the expression-like `(direction, name)` ordering key with classified prose stating that ports are ordered first by direction and then by name.
Replace the expression-like "(direction, name) order" with classified prose such as ordering first by direction and then by name.
Must the returned binding preserve the caller-chosen port order exactly, or must record_change canonicalize the ports into (direction, name) order?

quotes: propose_binding: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST return the one OperationBinding of the RecordSet record_change returns, which holds exactly the binding the ProposeBindingChange wrote, with status proposed and its ports in (direction, name) order; that record is returned as written and is never looked up again or matched against the proposal's ports, whose order the caller chose.
judgement.why: The tuple-like ordering key `(direction, name)` is an expression in a note, which the note-form rule forbids.

quotes: propose_binding: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST return the one OperationBinding of the RecordSet record_change returns, which holds exactly the binding the ProposeBindingChange wrote, with status proposed and its ports in (direction, name) order; that record is returned as written and is never looked up again or matched against the proposal's ports, whose order the caller chose.
judgement.why: The note identifies an enum member only through the value word `proposed` instead of naming the PROPOSED member beside the `= models.BindingStatus` address.

`the EXPENSE_CREATE member of = models.AuditAction`.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
